status: closed-partial: three real merged PRs plus a follow-up fix, two production deploys (the second superseding the first to also absorb P-159's concurrent fix), a live cross-lane deploy-traffic collision found and resolved. Two of three R-4 legs are independently confirmed PASS-worthy (refresh returns 202; export_instrument returns a real PDF on the first call, no retry, for both required probe parcels -- confirmed twice: once by this lane, once independently by the dispatch planner's own live MCP calls after this lane closed). The third leg (one browser click in Reports produces the PDF with no manual retry) has no authenticated Property Explorer session available to either this lane or the planner and is honestly UNMEASURED, not assumed. Per R-4, UNMEASURED is not a PASS; this row does not appear in any wave planRows.
missionPremise: F7 (OPS-23 section 2 / OPS-16 A-128, 2026-09-11): the engine completes feasibility composition in tens of seconds to several minutes (originally documented as 85-154s for Travis, 38-85s for Bastrop) while Property Explorer's BFF and smartsite-mcp both aborted at 55s under a 60s Vercel function cap, so a report that actually succeeded reached the customer as a fabricated 'cold start, try again' failure. Ruling: refresh becomes asynchronous (202 + job reference); both clients poll instead of holding the socket open.
completionPredicate: A stranger can evaluate this as done if: (1) POST .../feasibility-export/refresh returns 202 with a job reference instead of blocking; (2) a poller (PE's BFF, or smartsite-mcp's own internal poll) that checks back later gets the PDF for a job that kept running after the poller's own connection ended, with no failure ever shown for a job that later succeeds; (3) export_instrument feasibility returns a PDF for a probe parcel, either immediately (job already ready) or via a declared, non-error in-progress envelope followed by a PDF on a later call; (4) a job that genuinely fails lands in a `failed` state with a machine-readable errorClass, never silently `ready` and never silently deferred forever.
scopeBasis: Exactly the three repos and the one code path P-155 names (hauska-engine's feasibility-export routes; hauska-map's PE BFF + browser poll loop; legacy-design-tools/smartsite-mcp's export_instrument feasibility leg). P-159 (PDF content correctness) and P-152 (one-reader cutover) are adjacent, depended-on-by, or depend-on this row but are explicitly out of scope; the only P-159 interaction was a shared-service deploy collision (below), resolved without touching P-159's own code. The atom's closed `artifacts` type was deliberately not widened (substrate seat's call, found in-repo, not in the dispatch). No envelope-atom minting, no entitlement-gate change, no pricing-surface change, per the program's explicit prohibitions.

falsifier.preRegistered: Disconnect falsifier (mission step 2): start a job, disconnect immediately, poll three minutes later; if the state is not ready or failed, the design is wrong. MCP falsifier: if export_instrument feasibility 48453:474034 still returns no PDF after the deploy, or the app needs a manual retry for the same parcel, the row is not done. Non-vacuity falsifier: a job that throws must land in failed with an errorClass, never ready, never silently deferred.
falsifier.observed: Disconnect falsifier PASSED four separate times with real curl clients that moved on to poll rather than holding a connection open (149.1s, 213.8s, 54.0s, 629.6s wall times — see profile below); none stuck, all settled to ready. MCP falsifier PASSED via the real production connector (raw output above) with no manual retry required — a job whose accept the CLIENT aborted still completed server-side and was picked up on the next call. Non-vacuity falsifier PASSED in the unit suite (a mocked composition throw settles to failed with errorClass geometry_unavailable and 422s on download) but was NOT observed on a genuine live composition failure — none of the four live jobs actually failed, so this specific claim rests on test coverage, not a live occurrence, and should be said as such rather than implied to be live-proven.
